chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Sinan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who travels during the month of Ramadan and with him is a slave girl, and whether it is permissible for him to have intercourse with her during the day. He said: 'Glory be to Allah! Does he not recognize the sanctity of the month of Ramadan? For him, during the night, is a long duration.'

I said, 'Is it not for him that he can eat, drink, and shorten (the prayer)?' He said: 'Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has granted concession to the traveler regarding breaking the fast and shortening (the prayer) as a mercy and alleviation for the place of fatigue, exertion, and difficulty of travel. But He did not grant him concession regarding intercourse with women during the day while traveling in the month of Ramadan. He obligated upon him making up the fasts, and did not obligate upon him making up the complete prayers when he returns from his journey.'

Then he said: 'And the Sunnah cannot be measured by analogy, and I, whenever I travel during the month of Ramadan, do not eat except for the bare necessities, and do not drink until I quench my thirst completely.'
ai.seo_question: Can a traveler have sexual intercourse during the day in Ramadan?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the general concession for travelers to break the fast and shorten prayers and the specific prohibition of sexual intercourse during Ramadan days, emphasizing that the latter is not covered by the travel exemption. He highlights the sanctity of Ramadan nights ('sabhan tawilan') and illustrates the superior etiquette (adab) of the Sunnah, where the Prophet minimized consumption to mere sustenance rather than full satisfaction, distinguishing legal permissibility from spiritual excellence.
